name: nbody_force_scatter
task: This project simulates a small gravitational n-body system, split across multiple translation units: include/vec3.h (a header-only 3D vector), include/body.h + src/body.cpp (the Body type and a deterministic random-body generator), include/forces.h + src/forces.cpp (serial and OpenMP-parallel force computation that returns the potential energy), include/integrator.h + src/integrator.cpp (an explicit Euler time-stepping loop that can use either force routine), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). compute_forces_serial() visits each unordered pair (i, j) with j > i once and applies the force to both bodies (forces[i] += f; forces[j] -= f), accumulating the potential energy in a scalar. compute_forces_parallel() in src/forces.cpp runs the same loop nest under '#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 4)' on the outer index i, but iteration i also writes forces[j] for every j > i, i.e. entries owned by other iterations and other threads, and every iteration adds to the shared scalar 'energy', all without atomics, reductions or per-thread buffers. The concurrent read-modify-write updates are lost: the forces no longer match the serial result (or cancel to zero) and the energy is wrong, and simulate() in src/integrator.cpp inherits the error when it runs with parallel = true. Fix compute_forces_parallel() so forces and energy match the serial version within floating-point summation-order tolerance (the harness uses a relative tolerance of 1e-9) for any number of bodies and threads, while keeping the force loop parallelized with OpenMP (do not simply remove the pragma or serialize the loop; for example use per-thread force buffers that are merged afterwards plus an OpenMP reduction for the energy, or atomic updates, or compute the full j-loop per body without the symmetric update). Do not change any function signature declared in include/forces.h, include/body.h or include/integrator.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/app (src/main.cpp -> body.cpp, forces.cpp, integrator.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the parallel pair loop in compute_forces_parallel(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same body.cpp, forces.cpp, integrator.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
